sections.title: The letter i
paragraphs: The name of this letter is (i) /i/. It makes one main sound. You hear it in the word (itt) /ˈitː/, which means here. This letter makes one sound.

sections.title: Making the sound
paragraphs: To make this vowel, open your mouth only a little. A vowel is a sound made with open air and no touch in the mouth. Push your tongue high and forward. Spread your lips wide, like a gentle smile. Let the air flow through freely. Touch your throat to feel it shake.

sections.title: Reading the letter
paragraphs: This letter always makes the same sound in every position. You hear it at the start of (ing) /ˈiŋɡ/. You also hear it in (itt) /ˈitː/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not say this letter like the vowel in bit. That sound is too open and lax. Keep your tongue high and your lips spread wide, like the sound in see. Keep the sound short and steady.
